introH2: 🏙️ How many kinds of hotels are there in Ubon Ratchathani city, and how do you pick the right one for your trip?
introHtml: The phrase "a hotel in Ubon city" doesn't mean just one thing, and that's what makes choosing a place to stay here more fun than you'd expect — some are big hotels connected directly to a shopping mall, where you can walk from your room down to eat and catch a movie, with a water park for the kids. Some are arty design boutiques or small owner-run hotels that focus on cleanliness and quiet for a few hundred baht. And some still have a pool and a free airport shuttle even though they sit right in the middle of town. · A lot of people book a hotel in Ubon and end up with a location or facilities that don't match their own trip, and feel it wasn't worth it. · This article rounds up 10 hotels in Ubon Ratchathani city that we've reviewed in depth — the mall-connected side, the downtown area around Thung Si Mueang, and the side near the airport. Every one comes from reading real guest reviews, tells you both the upsides and the honest caveats, compares prices across 3 sites, and includes direct booking links throughout.
mrtHtml: There are several ways to get to Ubon Ratchathani. · By air is easiest: Ubon Ratchathani Airport (UBP) has several direct flights a day from Bangkok (Don Muang / Suvarnabhumi), about a 1-hour flight. · The airport is very close to the city, roughly a 5–15 min drive, and many city hotels offer an airport shuttle. · By train you arrive at Ubon Ratchathani Station (Warin Chamrap), and by intercity coach at the Ubon Ratchathani Bus Terminal (BKS). · Ubon has no metro; in town, calling a Grab or a hired car is easy, and if you drive yourself most of the hotels in this article have free parking. · Main areas to stay: around Thung Si Mueang, the heart of the old town, within walking distance of temples and the Ratchabut night market · Chayangkun Road on the north side of town, with malls and close to the airport · and the airport / Rai Noi side, quiet and good for people who fly in or drive themselves.

entries.name: Sunee Grand Hotel and Convention Center
entries.revCount: Trip.com 9.2 · 471 reviews · TripAdvisor #4 of 28 hotels in Ubon
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Connected to Sunee City Mall · City center · Airport 10 min
entries.addr: 512/8 Chayangkun Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani
entries.storyHtml: If there's one hotel that locals and travelers name first when asked for a place to stay in the city center, many reviews give it to this one — Sunee Grand Hotel and Convention Center is a 222-room 5-star city hotel connected directly to Sunee City Mall, the province's big shopping mall. It opened in 2009 and had a major renovation in 2022, with the highest score in this article at 9.2 from 471 reviews on Trip.com. · What makes people fall for it is the location: from the lobby you can walk straight into the mall — cinema, supermarket, restaurants, banks and a pharmacy — without stepping into the sun or calling a car. Many international reviewers use "convenient for shopping" and "easy to get around" as their favorite point. · The other highlight families talk about most is the outdoor water park and pool with a separate kids' pool and water play features that keep children happily occupied all afternoon, plus a gym, sauna, Thai-massage spa, and a large convention center that hosts seminars and weddings. · Rooms range from a Standard Double from about ฿900/night up to a Royal Suite with a living room and two bathrooms, and most reviews praise the spacious rooms, soft beds and cold, easy-to-adjust air-conditioning, especially the rooms renovated in 2022. · The honest caveat from the reviews: because it opened back in 2009, cleanliness and room condition aren't consistent across every room — there are reports of a musty smell or dust in some of the rooms not yet renovated, Wi-Fi that isn't steady in spots around the building, and a breakfast leaning toward Asian dishes that can feel repetitive over several nights. · The tip many reviews agree on is to request a renovated room (renovated 2022) when you book — it greatly cuts the chance of landing an older room. · This isn't a brand-new design hotel or a luxury riverside resort, but it's the best value for convenience for families who want a water park for the kids, businesspeople here for meetings, and anyone who wants everything on their trip within reach.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: When booking, request a renovated room (renovated 2022), and if you're traveling with kids ask for a room near the pool so getting to the water park is easy. · If you get tired of the breakfast menu, walk down into the mall — there are plenty of restaurants and a supermarket to choose from.
pros: Connected directly to Sunee City Mall — walk to the mall, cinema and supermarket
Water park and pool with a kids' pool, good for families traveling with children
Has it all: gym, spa, large convention center, free parking and an airport shuttle
Highest score in the article at 9.2 · good value for the location and facilities
cons: Open since 2009, so cleanliness and room condition aren't consistent across every room
Breakfast leans Asian; the menu can feel repetitive over several nights (from reviews)
Wi-Fi isn't steady in some spots of the building · a few extra charges to check first

entries.name: V Hotel Ubon Ratchathani
entries.revCount: Trip.com 9.2 · 117 reviews · TripAdvisor #5 of 28 hotels in Ubon
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chaeng Sanit Road · City center · Near Funtastic World
tags: 🅿️ Free covered parking in the building
entries.addr: 63 Chaeng Sanit Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani
entries.storyHtml: Among the hotels in Ubon city, if you measure value for money against room cleanliness, V Hotel Ubon Ratchathani is one of the most talked-about — a 4-star city hotel on Chaeng Sanit Road that opened in 2015, around 79 rooms in a clean, modern style, scoring 9.2 from 117 reviews on Trip.com and #5 of 28 hotels in Ubon on TripAdvisor. · What sets it apart from hotels at the same price is that it sells "value" first — the rooms aren't loudly decorated, but they're clean-lined, modern and well kept. · The thing guests agree on most in real reviews is the cleanliness and a room size larger than expected at this price: bright rooms, with housekeeping changing the linens and tidying every day. Many say "genuinely clean, not just clean at a glance." · Another standout is the free covered parking inside the building — roomy, easy and secure, which is one of the things self-drivers praise most, since parking is a hassle at many city hotels. · The location is right in the city center, walkable to Funtastic World Ubon, an indoor amusement park only about 80 m away, and Huai Muang Park about 200 m away, which makes it great for families with kids; the airport is about a 10-min drive. · The honest caveat: it has to be said up front that V Hotel has no pool, so if your trip has kids who want to swim you should consider a hotel with a pool instead. Breakfast is mostly a paid add-on with limited choices, the area's walkability is fairly low so without a car it feels inconvenient to get around, and some rooms get noise from the street or the room next door. · If your brief is a good, clean, value room where you sleep well and park easily for a sightseeing or work trip in Ubon, V Hotel hits that mark — and it's why so many guests say they'd come back.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're sensitive to noise, ask for a high floor or a side that doesn't face Chaeng Sanit Road. · Coming by car is easiest since parking is free in the building, and with limited breakfast at the hotel, try heading out for food around Chaeng Sanit Road — you'll get the real Ubon vibe and spend less.
pros: Very clean rooms, larger than expected at this price (the point reviews praise most)
Free covered parking in the building — convenient and secure
City-center location, walkable to Funtastic World and Huai Muang Park, good for families
Friendly, helpful staff who speak English · airport 10 min away
cons: No pool · not ideal if you have kids who want to swim
Breakfast is a paid add-on with limited choices · no other meal service
The area isn't great for walking without a car · some rooms get outside noise (from reviews)

entries.name: B2 Ubon Boutique & Budget Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Rai Noi area · Near Ubon airport (~15 min)
entries.addr: 499 Moo 12, Rai Noi, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani
entries.storyHtml: If you measure by the lowest starting price in this article, B2 Ubon Boutique & Budget Hotel is the one — part of the B2 Boutique & Budget Hotels chain, a budget brand with dozens of locations across Thailand. This Ubon branch in the Rai Noi area only opened in 2025, so both the rooms and the common areas are brand new — a real advantage among hotels at the same price, many of which are starting to show their age. It scores 9.0 from 223 reviews on Trip.com. · What guests agree on most is the rooms: many say they look freshly opened, with the chain's signature modern bright-toned design, no musty smell, clean linens and towels, beds that are soft just right, and air-conditioning that cools evenly — reflected in a cleanliness sub-score as high as about 9.4. · There are 4 room types, from a Superior for two friends up to a Family Suite that sleeps up to 5, good for families or groups who want to save by sharing one room. · It sits in the Rai Noi area on the airport side out of town, about 8 km from Ubon airport, roughly a 15-min drive, with free parking — great for anyone flying in and out or driving themselves. · The honest caveats to know before booking: the first one mentioned most is that the hotel has no lift — if you get a 2nd- or 3rd-floor room you'll carry your bags up the stairs yourself, which is tiring with a lot of luggage or for older travelers. The second is there's no pool, and the third is that the starting price doesn't include breakfast. · On top of that the location isn't in the middle of the tourist area, so without your own car getting into town means a taxi or a ride-hailing app. · If what you want is a new, clean, value bedroom near the airport with free parking, and you're not fussed about a lift, pool or in-house breakfast, this is one of the most well-rounded and best-value choices in Ubon.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The hotel has no lift, so if you have a lot of luggage or find stairs difficult, request a 1st-floor room when you book. · Groups often choose the Deluxe Triple or Family Suite for a big room at a good price, and plan on grabbing breakfast from the shops nearby since the starting price doesn't include it.
pros: New rooms opened in 2025, clean, soft beds, good cold air-con (cleanliness about 9.4)
Lowest starting price in the article, from about ฿550/night
Several room types, from solo to a family of 5 · free parking
Near Ubon airport, 24-hour front desk, good for flyers and self-drivers
cons: No lift; carrying bags up to the 2nd–3rd floor is tiring with a lot of stuff
Breakfast not included in the starting price · no pool
Not in the middle of the tourist area; you'll need a ride into town (from reviews)

entries.name: Rapeepan Ville Hotel
entries.revCount: Trip.com 9.4 · 41 reviews · TripAdvisor #3 in the B&B group in Ubon
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Near Ubon airport (~12 min) · On a quiet lane
entries.addr: 9 Soi Suk Upatham 11, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani
entries.storyHtml: If you measure by review score, Rapeepan Ville Hotel is the one with the highest score in this article at 9.4 on Trip.com, even though it's a small hotel in a secondary city — a family-run place of around 28 rooms tucked into Soi Suk Upatham 11 on the side near the airport. It opened around 2012, was renovated in 2015, and still ranks #3 of 37 B&B/guesthouse properties in Ubon on TripAdvisor. · What reviews agree on is that it makes cleanliness and quiet the heart of the place, rather than being a big chain hotel selling lots of facilities. · The highest-scoring sub-categories are cleanliness (about 9.7) and service (about 9.6). Many use the word "spotless," and the word "quiet" comes up on almost every page of reviews, because the lane sits a little off the main road so there's no busy traffic noise. · It's decorated in a warm contemporary Thai style, some rooms have a private balcony looking out over a small garden, and the buffet breakfast (about 150 baht extra) earns praise from many reviews for being tasty, with both Thai and Western dishes. · Service is the main charm — staff and the owner get repeated praise for being friendly, attentive and very helpful, with international guests mentioning "the boss" as warm and ready to help personally. · It's about 5 km from Ubon airport, roughly a 12-min drive, with an airport shuttle (for a fee) and free parking. · The honest caveats: this is a small hotel with no pool, so if that's a must-have you can rule it out; the soundproofing between rooms isn't great, so you sometimes hear the room next door; there's no lift, which makes upper-floor rooms hard for older travelers; and the location is a little outside the city center, so you'll need a ride into town. · For what it sets out to be — a small, clean, quiet hotel near the airport at a gentle price — Rapeepan Ville does it well and is genuinely good value, just as the reviews say.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Soundproofing between rooms isn't great, so if you're a light sleeper ask for a corner room or one that doesn't share a wall. · If you're flying in, give your flight time in advance to book the airport shuttle, and try the in-house breakfast — many reviews say it's tasty and good value.
pros: Highest score in the article at 9.4 · cleanliness about 9.7, service about 9.6
Very quiet and clean, good for anyone who wants to sleep well
Friendly, warm service, with the owner looking after guests personally (from reviews)
Near Ubon airport, with a shuttle and free parking · breakfast earns praise
cons: No pool · few facilities, as you'd expect from a small hotel
Soundproofing between rooms isn't great · no lift, so upper-floor rooms are hard
Location is a little outside the city center; you'll need a ride into town (from reviews)

entries.name: Excella Hotel
entries.revCount: Trip.com 8.6 · 72 reviews · TripAdvisor #1 in the Specialty category in Ubon
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chayangkun Road · Near Nong Bua Market · Airport 10 min
tags: 🛋️ Spacious suites, balcony in every room
entries.addr: 66/1 Soi Chayangkun 40, Chayangkun Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani
entries.storyHtml: If you have to stay in Ubon for several nights and want more space than a bare bedroom, Excella Hotel is the place guests bring up most for this — a small 3-star condo-style hotel of 57 rooms that positions itself between a "hotel" and an "apartment." It opened around 2013, scores 8.6 from 72 reviews on Trip.com, and holds TripAdvisor 4.3/5, ranked #1 of 30 Specialty lodging properties in Ubon. · The star of the show here, and what sets it apart from ordinary city hotels, is that every room is a suite with a sitting area separate from the bed, and crucially a kitchenette with a microwave, fridge, sink, dining table, and a private balcony in every room, so it feels like having a little home in the city. · Reviews strongly agree the rooms are very clean, the beds comfortable, and the rooms larger than the price suggests — and over several nights, being able to heat up your own food saves a fair bit on meals. · It's in the Chayangkun area, about a 10-min walk to Nong Bua Market, near Big C, and about a 10-min drive from Ubon airport, on a lane in a quiet residential area where you sleep well. · The honest caveats: Excella has no pool and no gym, so if those two are must-haves this may not be the pick. The location isn't in the middle of the restaurant area — several international reviewers say "a bit out of main area," so without a car you may rely on Grab to go out for food. Some feel breakfast still needs improvement, especially if you come down late, and the rooms have no tea/coffee set, so if you need coffee in the morning bring your own or use the in-room kitchenette to boil water. · For travelers staying in Ubon for several nights, families who want to heat up their own meals, and self-drivers who value usable space and quiet, Excella offers value that's hard to find at this price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Nong Bua Market and Big C are nearby, and every room has a kitchenette, so you can buy food and heat it up in your room easily and cheaply. · The rooms have no tea/coffee set, so if you need coffee in the morning bring sachets, and if you'll arrive after 8:00 PM, tell the hotel ahead to arrange key pickup.
pros: Every room is a spacious suite with a kitchenette, fridge, microwave and private balcony
TripAdvisor #1 in Specialty lodging in Ubon · good for long stays where you cook for yourself
Very clean rooms, quiet area where you sleep well · free parking out back
Near Ubon airport and walkable to Nong Bua Market · friendly staff
cons: No pool and no gym
Location is away from the city center and restaurants; you'll want a car or a Grab
No tea/coffee set in the rooms · breakfast still has room to improve (from reviews)

entries.name: Pentahug Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Wat Nong Bua area · Near Ubon bus terminal (~10 min)
entries.addr: 13 Soi Suk Upatham 9, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani
entries.storyHtml: If you arrive by coach at the Ubon bus terminal, or you're here on business around Wat Nong Bua, and you want a place with more of a design feel than an ordinary hotel at a reasonable price, Pentahug Hotel (officially Pen Ta Hug Hotel) is a name reviews mention often — a 3-star boutique hotel of around 79–82 rooms that stands apart from typical budget hotels in town by leaning into arty decor, with wall paintings, bright colors and common areas laid out with intent. It scores 8.6 on Trip.com, with a high service sub-score of about 9.0. · What guests bring up most is the decor — each room has wall paintings and bold use of color that make the room feel lively and good for photos, not the plain white box you usually find. · Service is the strength that earns the most consistent praise: front-desk staff are described as cheerful, friendly, quick to respond and willing to help, whether recommending restaurants, calling a car, or helping arrange a room change. · There's a shady green garden, a bike rental service, and a Thai/fusion restaurant with a coffee shop. · The location is about a 10-min drive from the Ubon bus terminal, about 5 min from Wat Phra That Nong Bua and Ubon Ratchabhat University, and around 5–6 km from the airport. · The honest caveats from the reviews: the one mentioned most is the mattress and bedding in some rooms starting to age or being too firm — some people get a sore back, so it's worth asking to try the room or to switch. Next is inconsistent water pressure and temperature in some rooms and noisy air-con in spots; there's no lift, so an upper-floor room means stairs; no pool; and the buffet breakfast is a paid add-on (about 140 baht), not included in the starting price. · If what you want is a place with style, a good vibe, lovely staff, near the bus terminal, and you're not fussed about a possibly firm mattress or a flight of stairs, Pentahug is a charming, good-value option in Ubon.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Some reviews mention firm mattresses, so if you're sensitive to that, ask to try the room or request a recently refurbished one at check-in. · The hotel has no lift, so if you have a lot of stuff ask for a lower-floor room, and breakfast is a paid add-on of about 140 baht, or walk out to the shops and 7-Eleven nearby.
pros: Distinctive art design with wall paintings, great for photos, different from hotels at the same price
Warm service, quick to respond (service about 9.0) · shady garden and bike rental
Near the Ubon bus terminal, Wat Nong Bua and Ubon Ratchabhat · free parking
Has a Thai/fusion restaurant and coffee shop, with shops and a 7-Eleven within walking distance
cons: Mattresses in some rooms are aging or too firm; some get a sore back (from reviews)
No lift and no pool
Breakfast not included in the starting price · not in the middle of the tourist area, you'll need a car

entries.name: T3 House
entries.revCount: Trip.com 8.3 · 132 reviews · TripAdvisor #3 of 28 hotels in Ubon
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Sapphasit Road · Walk to Wat Chaeng + Thung Si Mueang
tags: 🧼 Clean rooms, big bathroom, strong hot water
🚶 Walk to Wat Chaeng and Thung Si Mueang
entries.addr: 1/1 Soi Sapphasit 1, Sapphasit Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani
entries.storyHtml: If you come to Ubon wanting a clean, quiet, private place for a few hundred baht in the city center, but don't want to sleep in a big tower hotel where nobody knows your face, T3 House is a name guests mention often — a small 76-room hotel in Soi Sapphasit 1, owner-run, opened in 2012, scoring about 8.3 and ranked #3 of 28 hotels in Ubon on TripAdvisor with a 4.2/5 rating, which is a strong showing for its size. · A distinctive selling point that's not easy to find at this price is that every room has a private balcony — many people love sitting out for the breeze, having morning coffee, or drying laundry. · What real reviews agree on most is the cleanliness of the rooms, comfortable beds, and a spacious bathroom with a strong hot-water shower, which many say exceeds expectations for a hotel at this price. · But the heart of why T3 House scores above its weight is the service — the owner looks after guests personally, chats warmly, and genuinely helps with trip planning, from recommending restaurants and giving directions to tips on Sam Phan Bok, Pha Taem or Kaeng Saphue, which makes many guests feel like they're staying at a friend's place. · The location is central, about 170 m to Wat Chaeng and about 8 min to Thung Si Mueang, around 2.3 km from Ubon airport, with free parking. · The honest caveats: the thing mentioned most is that the small sign and Soi Sapphasit 1 are hard to find the first time, especially at night, so pin the map beforehand. There's no in-room safe, which worries some about valuables; there's no kettle or microwave in the room; and being a small hotel, there's no pool and no full buffet breakfast. · For a city sightseeing or business trip in Ubon where you want cleanliness, quiet and a friendly feel at an accessible price, T3 House delivers — and it's why it has held a top spot in town for years.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The small sign and the lane are hard to find the first time, especially at night, so pin the map and note the hotel's number beforehand. · There's no in-room safe, so keep valuables on you or leave them at the front desk, and grab coffee from the café downstairs and bring it up to sip on the balcony in the morning.
pros: Every room has a private balcony, a standout that's hard to find at this price
Very clean rooms, big bathroom, strong hot-water shower, comfortable beds
Friendly owner and team who genuinely recommend places to go (the point reviews praise most)
Central location, walkable to Wat Chaeng and Thung Si Mueang · free parking · TripAdvisor #3
cons: Small sign and a hard-to-find lane the first time, especially at night
No in-room safe, no kettle or microwave · limited storage in some rooms
No pool and no buffet breakfast · some staff speak little English

entries.name: Tohsang City Hotel
entries.revCount: Trip.com 8.6 · Booking 8.7 · TripAdvisor #6 of 28 hotels in Ubon
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Phalochai Road · City center · Airport 10 min

rooms.type: Grand Deluxe Room (28 sq m, with balcony)

entries.addr: 251 Phalochai Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani
entries.storyHtml: When it comes to Ubon's local hotel brands, the name Tohsang is well known to locals from its riverside resort at Khong Chiam, and Tohsang City Hotel (now using the name Tohsang Heritage Ubon) is the in-town branch on Phalochai Road, a quiet residential area in the city center — a small hotel of around 33 rooms decorated in a contemporary vintage style with natural materials and craftwork, scoring 8.6 on Trip.com and 8.7 on Booking. · If there's one thing that gets Tohsang City Hotel talked about most, it's breakfast — reviews in many languages agree almost in one voice that breakfast here is done well, with international reviewers going as far as calling it "the best breakfast I've had in Thailand." What they praise is the mix of a Thai buffet, Western dishes and made-to-order items, with local Isan food to try too. · The next standout is the room cleanliness many rank first, and the residential quiet that Western reviews say means even in the city the rooms are so quiet you barely hear the street, so you sleep well. · Rooms range from a Superior at 25 sq m up to a King Suite at 48 sq m, and the one many recommend is the Grand Deluxe with a balcony, since the price difference is small but you get extra sitting space. · It's about 4 km from Ubon airport, with an airport shuttle and free parking, and works well as a base before heading on to Khong Chiam and Pha Taem. · The honest caveats: first is aircraft noise — because the hotel is near the airport and under the flight path, you sometimes hear planes passing, so light sleepers should ask for an interior room. Second, the decor and furniture look classic, leaning older, which won't suit fans of very modern design; some buildings have no lift, and there are few restaurants within walking distance, so you'll need a car. · For anyone who values cleanliness, quiet, good breakfast and value for money, Tohsang City Hotel is a well-rounded choice in Ubon.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The hotel is near the airport and you sometimes hear planes passing, so request an interior room not facing the airport when you book. · Don't miss breakfast, the thing guests praise most, and for dinner allow for a ride to Thung Si Mueang or a night market where there's more to eat.
pros: Breakfast earns praise from reviews in many languages, with Thai, Western and made-to-order dishes
Quiet and clean, with rooms quiet enough to sleep well even in the city (from reviews)
Warm contemporary vintage design · friendly service like a small hotel
Airport 10 min away, with a shuttle and free parking · usable as a base for Khong Chiam
cons: Near the airport; you sometimes hear planes passing
Some of the decor and furniture look classic, leaning older
Some buildings have no lift · few restaurants within walking distance, you'll need a car (from reviews)

entries.name: Laithong Hotel
entries.revCount: Trip.com 8.0 · 38 reviews · TripAdvisor #10 of 28 hotels in Ubon
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Phichit Rangsan Road · Thung Si Mueang area · Airport 5 min
entries.addr: 50 Phichit Rangsan Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani
entries.storyHtml: Most hotels in central Ubon are tall buildings with no pool, but Laithong Hotel is the exception — it's in the city center on Phichit Rangsan Road, walkable to Thung Si Mueang and the Ratchabut night market, only minutes from the airport, yet still has an outdoor pool, a kids' pool, and a free airport shuttle all in one place, a set of upsides that's hard to find in the same area. · It's a 4-star boutique hotel of about 124 rooms, established a while ago, with some rooms renovated in 2024, scoring about 8.0 on Trip.com. · What guests agree on most is the location: the hotel is only about 2 km from Ubon airport, just a 5–7 min drive, with a free airport shuttle and free parking, convenient for both flyers and self-drivers. · The next thing they praise is the spacious rooms, high ceilings, and large windows that let in plenty of natural light, a detail that's hard to find in a hotel at this price; some rooms have a separate sitting area. · The honest caveats to know before booking: room quality isn't consistent and depends on whether you get a renovated room or an original one — original rooms show wear with the building's age and some have a musty smell. The thing to watch most is that the pool is both a highlight and the biggest thing to watch — a number of reviews complain that at times the water isn't clear, looks green or has a smell, and the real condition doesn't match the promotional photos, which suggests pool upkeep isn't consistent year-round. So if you plan to let the kids swim, walk over and check the pool with your own eyes before deciding. · It's notable that people who get a renovated room tend to rate it highly and feel it's good value, while those who get an old room tend to complain about the condition. · If you're after a value place in central Ubon that gets you the location, a pool, and friendly service, Laithong is a well-rounded option — just pick the right room and set your expectations accordingly.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: When booking, request a room renovated in 2024 (usually the Deluxe), since the condition is clearly different from the original rooms. · If you plan to let the kids swim, walk over and check the pool water with your own eyes first, don't go by the photos alone, and give your flight time in advance to book the free airport shuttle.
pros: One of the city hotels in Ubon that still has an outdoor pool and a kids' pool, good for families
Free airport shuttle and free parking · airport just a 5–7 min drive away
Spacious rooms, high ceilings, large windows for good light · 2024-renovated rooms are in better shape
City-center location, walkable to Thung Si Mueang and the night market · good service
cons: Room quality isn't consistent; old rooms show wear and some have a musty smell
Pool upkeep is inconsistent at times, with water that isn't clear (from reviews)
Cleanliness isn't consistent in some rooms · request a renovated room first

entries.type: Convention 3-Star · With an On-Site Water Park
entries.name: Nevada Convention Hotel
entries.revCount: TripAdvisor 3.4/5 · 16 reviews · #14 of 28 hotels in Ubon
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chayangkun Road · Near Ubon airport (~10 min)
entries.addr: 434 Chayangkun Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani
entries.storyHtml: If you're looking for a place in Ubon where the kids can swim all day without going anywhere, or you need to run a seminar or Chinese-banquet dinner and want guests staying in the same building, Nevada Convention Hotel is a name locals have known for a long time — a large, veteran 150-room convention hotel on Chayangkun Road near Ubon airport, open since 2003 and with a major renovation in 2019, rated about 3.4 of 5 on TripAdvisor, #14 of 28 hotels in Ubon. · The main selling point that sets it apart from other hotels in town is the Nevada Water Park on the same grounds, with both indoor and outdoor pools, a kids' pool and water play features, so families can let the kids swim all day, plus large meeting and banquet halls that hold seminars, weddings and Chinese-banquet dinners for several hundred people. · What reviews agree on is the spacious rooms and big bathrooms, an upside of an older building laid out larger than newer towers, and the roomy free parking, about a 10-min drive from the airport. · It has to be said up front that the review scores here are fairly split, with opinions clearly divided into two camps more than at a typical hotel. · The honest caveats from the critical side: the thing mentioned most is the building and rooms looking old for their age, with some comparing parts to something built long ago despite the 2019 renovation. Next is fairly firm beds, air-con that doesn't get fully cold or has dust in some rooms in the hot season, Wi-Fi that's unstable in spots, an outdoor pool with little shade that gets harsh sun midday, and some older reviews mentioning a musty smell and insects in some rooms. · The takeaway is that people who understand they're staying at a veteran hotel built for space and activities tend to be satisfied, while those expecting newness and polish tend to be disappointed — setting the right expectations is the single most important thing. · If you're a family who wants the kids to swim, a seminar/event organizer, or a group that values space and full facilities all in one place, Nevada is an easy-to-understand, value choice.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The outdoor pool and water park get harsh sun midday with little shade, so swimming in the morning or evening is more comfortable, and check the water park's opening hours when you book. · The older building has rooms in varying condition, so ask for the most recently renovated room and check the smell, dust and air-con right when you check in — you can ask to switch if you hit a problem.
pros: Has the on-site Nevada Water Park with indoor-outdoor pools and a kids' pool, swim all day
Large meeting and banquet halls for seminars and Chinese-banquet dinners of several hundred
Spacious rooms, big bathrooms · roomy free parking, near the airport
Accessible price, good value for families and groups who use the facilities fully
cons: The building and rooms look old for their age despite the 2019 renovation · beds are fairly firm

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting prices from the standard room range and may change by date and season; we recommend checking the real price and comparing 3 sites before every booking. · The scores and highlights in this article come from reading real guest reviews on booking platforms — we did not stay ourselves. · Tohsang City Hotel now uses the name Tohsang Heritage Ubon — it's the same place. · During the Candle Festival (around July), Ubon's annual highlight, as well as long holidays and times with big conventions, prices rise and rooms sell out very fast, so book several weeks ahead. · Ubon has no metro; Grab or a hired car is easy, and from Ubon airport (UBP) into town is about 5–15 min. · Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — questions travelers ask most about hotels in Ubon Ratchathani city

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best hotel in Ubon Ratchathani city?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style. · By score, Rapeepan Ville Hotel has the highest in the article at 9.4, a small, quiet, clean hotel near the airport. · If you want a location walkable to the mall with a water park for the kids, Sunee Grand Hotel connects directly to Sunee City Mall. · If you want a clean value room with parking, V Hotel. · For a long stay with a kitchen, Excella Hotel. · And if you want a pool in the city center, Laithong Hotel

faq.q: ❓ How much do hotels in Ubon city cost?
faq.a: In this article prices start at about ฿550–1,200 per night. · The most accessible are B2 Ubon and T3 House from ฿550. · Mid-range are Nevada ฿650, Excella ฿700, Laithong ฿700, V Hotel ฿800, Rapeepan Ville ฿800 and Pentahug ฿850. · And Sunee Grand from ฿900 and Tohsang City Hotel from ฿1,200. · All prices are approximate starting prices from standard rooms, and during the Candle Festival prices may be higher than usual

faq.q: ❓ Which area is best to stay in Ubon Ratchathani city?
faq.a: Around Thung Si Mueang (Sapphasit / Phichit Rangsan Road) is good for those who want to walk to temples and the Ratchabut night market (T3 House, Laithong). · Chayangkun Road on the north side of town has malls and is near the airport (Sunee Grand, Excella, Nevada). · The airport / Rai Noi side is quiet, good for flyers and self-drivers (B2 Ubon, Rapeepan Ville). · And the Wat Nong Bua / Chaeng Sanit area is near the bus terminal and Funtastic World (Pentahug, V Hotel)

faq.q: ❓ Which hotels in Ubon city have a pool?
faq.a: Most hotels in Ubon city are in-town buildings with no pool, but three in this article have one. · Sunee Grand Hotel has a water park and a kids' pool with water play features. · Laithong Hotel is a city hotel that still has an outdoor pool and a kids' pool (though upkeep is inconsistent at times, so walk over and check the condition first). · And Nevada Convention Hotel has the on-site Nevada Water Park with both indoor and outdoor pools, good for families letting the kids swim

faq.q: ❓ Which hotel in Ubon city is good for families traveling with kids?
faq.a: The most family-focused are the hotels with a pool for the kids to swim. · Sunee Grand Hotel has a water park and kids' pool, walkable to the mall and cinema. · Nevada Convention Hotel has the on-site Nevada Water Park to swim all day. · Laithong Hotel has a pool and kids' pool in the city center. · And B2 Ubon and Excella have family rooms / spacious suites that sleep several at good value, good if you're not fussed about a pool

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should you book a hotel in Ubon?
faq.a: Many hotels in this article are small properties (28–150 rooms), so they fill up fast during busy times. · During the Candle Festival (around July), Ubon's annual highlight, as well as long holidays, book several weeks to 1–2 months ahead because the city fills up and rooms sell out very fast. · In normal periods 1–2 weeks is enough. · Every platform has Free Cancellation, so we recommend locking a price like that first if your plans aren't firm, then comparing Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price
